content.content: The viewer shall express selection emphasis so that dimming or brightening elements adds no per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element presentation, compositing, paint, layout, style-recalculation or traversal work when the viewport moves or scales: applying one and the same viewport change under active selection emphasis costs the same through to the displayed surface however many elements the emphasis dims or brightens.
content.rationale:
vztxmxum settles that a user interaction's cost follows what that interaction changed, not the number of nodes visible in the panel. A viewport change — panning or zooming — changes only the viewport transform, yet when selection emphasis is active the dimmed set typically spans the unselected elements on screen and therefore grows with the visible graph. Writing emphasis incrementally when selection changes and writing only a single viewport transform when the viewport moves or scales is not by itself enough to hold the prerequisite's bound: if dimming or brightening is expressed through a presentation primitive that causes the host to recomposite, repaint, blend, recalculate styles or lay out each dimmed or brightened element whenever the viewport transform changes, then the host's presentation work on every viewport change scales with the dimmed or brightened set and therefore with the number of visible nodes. This node closes that path by committing how selection emphasis is expressed across a viewport change.

Expression and mechanism. Selection emphasis — both the dimming of unselected elements and the brightening or highlighting of selected and related elements — is expressed exclusively through presentation properties that settle when selection changes and remain passive while the viewport moves or scales. Dimming and brightening are represented in the already-rendered appearance of the affected elements (such as their resolved fill, stroke or text colors) or in a fixed number of shared layers that does not grow with the dimmed or brightened set, and never through per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element compositing groups, per-element opacity or filter stacking surfaces, per-element blend passes, or styles and attributes that must be re-evaluated when an ancestor viewport transform changes. Because the expression of emphasis introduces no per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element surface or pass for the host to process during a transform update, a viewport change neither walks nor updates the dimmed or brightened elements in the viewer's own code and provokes no per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element style recalculation, layout, paint or compositing work in the host.

Full viewport-change cost. The bound covers the entire cost of a viewport change under active selection emphasis, from the input that changes the viewport through the viewport-transform write and all host presentation, style-recalculation, layout, paint and compositing work through to the displayed surface. It does not stop at bounding the selection-change step that initially applies or clears emphasis, and it does not stop at the single write that updates the viewport transform. Every per-dimmed-element and per-brightened-element term between the viewport update and the displayed pixels is excluded: when the viewport moves or scales, the work performed by both the viewer and the host is invariant to how many elements the active selection emphasis dims or brightens.

Licence and non-contradiction. The commitment elaborates vztxmxum rather than restating it: vztxmxum states the general cost relation between an interaction and the visible node count, whereas this node specifies how selection emphasis must be expressed so that a viewport change while emphasis is active satisfies that relation end to end. Every clause is licensed directly by vztxmxum's requirement that applying the same change costs the same whether few or many nodes are visible. Nothing in the prerequisite is contradicted or weakened — the interactive HTML page in the VS Code panel remains intact, and no viewport change is permitted to scale in cost with the dimmed, brightened or visible element count.

No substitute goal. The commitment is satisfied by how selection emphasis is expressed, not by trading away interactivity or substituting a different target. It sets no frame-rate target, no latency budget, and no element-count or node-count ceiling or threshold; it does not throttle, coalesce away, skip or drop viewport updates; and it adopts no rendering or visual technique, library, file, protocol or host for its own sake apart from keeping viewport-change cost independent of the number of dimmed or brightened elements.

Decidability. The commitment is decidable from this recorded statement alone without any external rule: a refuting observation is either two occurrences of the same viewport change under active selection emphasis with different numbers of dimmed or brightened elements whose full cost through to the displayed surface differs, or an emphasis expression that introduces a per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element walk, update, style recalculation, layout, paint or compositing pass on a viewport change. The node records the commitment, not any runtime measurement or verdict.
